brief: Deutsche Bank's morning macro note. A weekend show of agreement among prominent AI leaders that safety and oversight lag capability drove Asian risk-off: KOSPI -2.74%, SK Hynix -6.60%, Softbank -11.24%, NASDAQ 100 futures -1.25%. Reid argues the debate alters the composition of AI capex toward safety and governance rather than its scale, because the competitive race between companies and countries makes voluntary restraint unlikely, a reading Trump supported by opposing any pause. Brent rose 2.82% to $107.56 after a precautionary Saudi pipeline shutdown and the postponement of Iran-Gulf talks on a Hormuz shipping corridor. Last week's chain ran energy surge (Brent +8.65%, European gas +10.52%) to stagflation fears and faster-hike speculation, then to a global sovereign selloff, US 2yr +25.9bps to 4.63% and the bund at a post-2009 high of 3.50%, then to S&P 500 -0.80% cushioned by Mag 7 +0.63%. DB expects a 25bp Fed hike Wednesday to 3.75%-4.00%, market pricing 87%, and has added a March hike for 75bps over seven months, supported by August core CPI at 0.29% and estimated core PCE at 0.27%. It sees the BoE on hold at 3.75% with a 6-3 split and the BoJ hiking 25bp.
